newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soy exports forecast 10.6 pct all exports.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soy exports forecast 10.6 pct all exports.

text.p: Exports of Brazilian soybeans and soyproducts should represent 10.6 percent of total Brazilian exports in 1997, up from 9.3 percent in 1996 and the highest since 1989, said consultants Safras e Mercado.
Exports of soybeans alone should generate $2.32 billion in revenue, 128 percent up on last year and equivalent to 43 percent of revenue from the whole complex, Safras said in a weekly report.

The largest income is still expected to come from soymeal exports which are forecast to reach $2.62 billion in value, down from $2.73 billion in 1996 but representing 48 percent of total soycomplex sales forecast at $5.41 billion.
According to Safras, some 4.05 million tonnes of soybeans had been exported between February 1 and June 9 against 1.95 million tonnes to the same stage last year.

Soymeal shipments to June 9 were lagging behind 1996, reaching 3.43 million tonnes against 4.11 million last year and soyoil exports were virtually unchanged at 478,400 tonnes compared with 483,100 tonnes in 1996.
Around 58 percent of soybean exports and 35 percent of soymeal shipments between January and May this year went to the Netherlands, Safras said.
China which last year during the same period was the ninth largest receiver of soymeal has this year jumped to third place.
China was also responsible for buying 49 percent of Brazilian soyoil exports during January to May, Safras said.
